name: Paolo Bulgari
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Paolo Bulgari, a great-grandson of the founder of luxury jeweler Bulgari, joined the company when he was 18.
A law student at the time, he was asked by his father to design necklaces, rings and bracelets.
Paolo became chairman of Bulgari in 1984, while his brother Nicola became vice chairman.
In 2011, the Bulgari family sold its controlling stake to French luxury conglomerate LVMH for $5.2 billion in cash and stock.
forbes_facts: Paolo has designed jewelry for generations of Hollywood actresses, from Elizabeth Taylor to Nicole Kidman.
Bulgari financed a year-long restoration project of the Spanish Steps in Rome for a reported $1.6 million and wants restricted access to the monument to protect it.

name: John Hancock
forbes_bio: John Hancock is the eldest child of Australia's richest woman, Gina Rinehart.
Together with his three sisters, Bianca, Hope and Ginia, he is the beneficiary of a trust that owns a large stake in mining giant Hancock Prospecting.
He is involved in a bitter court battle to take control of the trust from his mother and potentially increase their stake.
He is a senior adviser at Lind Partners LLC. He also runs his own private investment fund.
Hancock disclosed that as of September 2023 it had provided A$5.44 billion for dividends that will be paid after the dispute between Bianca and her brother John against their mother is resolved.
forbes_facts: He changed his surname from Rinehart to Hancock at age 27, after his grandfather, mining mogul Lang Hancock.
Hancock finished school at the prestigious Phillips Academy in Andover, Massachusetts.

name: O. Francis Biondi
forbes_bio: O. Francis Biondi cofounded hedge fund King Street Capital Management in 1995 with fellow First Boston alum Brian Higgins.
King Street Capital Management oversees over $25 billion in assets and focuses on out-of-favor investments in stocks and bonds.
Biondi retired from King Street in 2020, but kept his ownership stake in the firm.
forbes_facts: Biondi and Higgins also run the King Street Charitable Trust, whose grant recipients include his alma mater Yale, Memorial Sloan Kettering and others.
He's married to Jamie Nicholls, a former Forstmann Little partner and alum of Amherst College.

name: James France
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: James France inherited an estimated 36% of Nascar, the stock-car racing business founded in 1948 by his father, William France Sr.
He has sat on Nascar's board of directors since 2000.
Viewership is down, but the business remains afloat due to 7-year TV deals with Fox, NBC, Amazon Prime Video, and TNT, worth $7.7 billion in rights, that began in 2025.
France also serves as chairman of Nascar's sister company, International Speedway Corp, which operates 13 racetracks.
After Sprint's contracted ended in December 2016, Nascar signed a $20 million per year deal with Monster Energy that commenced in 2017.
forbes_facts: His niece Lesa France Kennedy is International Speedway's CEO, while nephew Brian France is Nascar's chief executive.
France raced in the U.S. Motorcycle Grand Prix in the late 1960s, raced dirt track competitions for nearly five years and has raced karts on both dirt and asphalt.

name: Konstantin Diehl
forbes_bio: Konstantin Diehl is a member of the fourth generation and holds a leadership role as the Deputy Chairman of the Supervisory Board.
The Nuremberg, Germany, based family enterprise is a global technology leader, generating annual sales of more than $5 billion.
The group's diversified portfolio includes strategic sectors such as Metall, Controls, Defence, Aviation, and Hydrometering.
The Diehl Group employs a workforce of more than 18,000 people across its various international divisions.
Originally founded in 1902 as a specialised foundry, the company has evolved over four generations into a major international industrial group.

name: Arsen Kanokov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Arsen Kanokov's fortune stems from the Sindika Group, which has 35 shopping centers in southern Russia and eight hotels -- three of which are in Sochi, a prominent city known for its resorts.
Kanokov was born in Kabardino-Balkaria, in 2005-2013 he used to be a president of Kabardino-Balkaria, one of Russia southern regions.
He is a member of the Federation Council from Kabardino-Balkarian Republic.
Kanokov bought shares of Starbucks, OBI and McDonalds in Russia after the companies decided to exit the country amid the Russia-Ukraine war.
He is under E.U. and U.S. sanctions since 2022, and under U.K. sanctions since 2025.

name: Thomas Lau
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2015-2020); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Thomas Lau is chairman and CEO of Lifestyle International, a shopping-mall outfit whose Sogo flagship anchors the city's pricey Causeway Bay district.
He sits on the board of Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
His brother, Joseph, is also a billionaire. They both collect art.
In November 2020 Lifestyle International announced plans to purchase the London headquarters of oil giant BP for more than $330 million.

name: Juan Domingo Beckmann Legorreta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Juan Domingo Beckmann Legorreta inherited a nearly 51% stake in tequila firm Becle S.A.B., maker of Jose Cuervo, from his father Juan Francisco Beckmann.
The company went public on the Mexican Stock Exchange in 2017 under Juan Domingo's leadership. He remains CEO.
Founded in 1758, Becle has remained family-owned for over 250 years.
His sister Karen Beckmann Legorreta inherited nearly 36% of the company from their father and is a billionaire as well.
forbes_facts: La Rojeña, built by the Cuervo family in 1812, is Latin America's oldest active distillery.
In 2022, Beckmann partnered with comedian Kevin Hart to create the Gran Coramino tequila brand.

name: Wang Shih-Chung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Shih-Chung is the chairman of Taiwan's AirTAC International Group, a maker of pneumatic equipment for the automotive, electronics, medical and other sectors.
He worked at a factory upon graduating high school, and set up the company in 1988.
AirTAC is headquartered in Taipei with a strong foothold in mainland China, where it has two manufacturing sites.
